primary_category.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: the reactor operator flagged that feedwater pump 1B's discharge pressure had a slow upward oscillation... I had him log it and bump up the monitoring interval
evidence.explanation: The supervisor gathers instrument data, evaluates its significance against normal band/alarm criteria, and decides on a monitoring response, a core information-evaluation act.

evidence.quote: Pulling the historical vibration comparison off the plant computer was something I could've done — the data was right there — but... it didn't feel necessary in that window.
evidence.explanation: The episode centers on whether to retrieve and evaluate available comparative data before deciding to continue or hold, an explicit information-search/evaluation task.

evidence.quote: I pulled the historical comparison myself later that shift... The comparison showed the rate of climb didn't quite match the earlier benign cases.
evidence.explanation: Direct act of retrieving and evaluating historical trend data to assess a technical condition.

evidence.quote: he said it looked consistent with known control response at that power level
evidence.explanation: Interpreting the level blip requires applying a mental model of expected control-system behavior at a given power level, i.e., diagnostic abstraction rather than mere data lookup.

evidence.quote: The item that ends up mattering isn't always the one making noise — sometimes it's the one you've already decided you understand.
evidence.explanation: The participant generalizes a principle about attention and understanding from the specific incident, indicating abstraction/learning.

evidence.quote: I had three things going — the pump, the pre-brief prep, and the ascension clock.
evidence.explanation: The supervisor must sequence and prioritize competing tasks and timelines (pump monitoring, pre-brief preparation, ascension schedule), which involves organizing resources and contingencies toward multiple goals.
Setting a contingent escalation criterion reflects forward-looking planning for a non-routine trajectory, not just executing a fixed script.

evidence.quote: I had him log it and bump up the monitoring interval
evidence.explanation: The supervisor directs the reactor operator's actions, allocating monitoring tasks, evidencing a coordinating/supervisory role.

evidence.quote: I called our on-call reactor engineer, walked him through it
evidence.explanation: The supervisor coordinates across roles (operator, engineer) to align understanding and next steps during the evolving situation.

not_observed_or_insufficient: A1.1 Strength - no evidence of physical exertion
A1.2 Dexterity - no manual instrument manipulation described
A1.3 Navigation - no physical movement through the environment described
A2.1 Uncodified visual/auditory processing - instrument readings are described as quantified band/alarm values rather than uncodified perceptual pattern recognition
A2.2 Literacy - logging is mentioned but not elaborated as a substantive literacy task
A2.3 Numeracy - percentages and band positions are referenced but no active calculation or quantitative reasoning is shown
A3.1 Serving and attending - no direct service-to-client interaction
A3.2 Teaching, training, and coaching - the closing advice to a 'newer supervisor' is reflective commentary in the debrief, not an in-episode teaching act
A3.3 Selling and influencing - no persuasion or negotiation observed
A3.5 Caring - no welfare-oriented support observed
ambiguities: A2.1 vs A2.4: instrument trend interpretation ('slow upward oscillation', 'upper third of its normal band') has a perceptual/pattern component but is described in explicitly quantified band terms, so it was classified under A2.4 rather than A2.1 due to lack of evidence of uncodified perceptual judgment.

A3.2 was considered for the closing advice-giving turn but rejected because it is meta-commentary to the interviewer about a hypothetical newer supervisor, not an observed in-task teaching act during the shift.

evidence.quote: I told the crew to keep it on the standard continue-and-monitor watch we use for that kind of trend, and we carried on toward the next hold point.
evidence.explanation: The supervisor independently selects the monitoring response, escalation timing, and whether to hold the ascension, without evidence of requiring prior approval.

evidence.quote: no real trend history to speak of... Still no tech spec limit reached, no alarm.
evidence.explanation: Decisions are bounded by formal technical-specification limits and alarm thresholds, and the pump eventually enters a formal tech-spec close-monitoring action, indicating externally defined compliance constraints on the work.

evidence.quote: I had him log it... I called our on-call reactor engineer, walked him through it
evidence.explanation: The supervisor works through the reactor operator and consults the on-call engineer, but the core evaluative decisions remain the supervisor's individual responsibility.

evidence.quote: Ascensions like this usually throw a couple small things at you — nothing alarming, just things worth tracking. That's what happened here.
evidence.explanation: The participant frames the type of minor developing issue as a recurring pattern in this kind of evolution.

evidence.quote: the continue-and-monitor watch we use for that kind of trend
evidence.explanation: A prescribed, named response protocol exists for this category of trend and is invoked directly.

evidence.quote: Still no tech spec limit reached, no alarm. But it had been trending the same direction for a while
evidence.explanation: Formal limits and bands provide predictable thresholds, but the eventual trajectory of the trend (and its divergence from prior cases) was not fully certain at the time.

evidence.quote: two developing items at once gets your attention
evidence.explanation: The concurrence of two atypical developing conditions during a routine evolution required the supervisor to respond beyond the purely scripted path, though ultimately resolved via engineer consultation.

tools.role_in_task: Plant computer historical trend library used to retrieve and compare vibration data.

evidence.quote: Pulling the historical vibration comparison off the plant computer... The comparison showed the rate of climb didn't quite match the earlier benign cases.
evidence.explanation: A special-purpose plant monitoring/historical-trend system, distinct from ordinary office software, is used to evaluate technical equipment data.

tools.role_in_task: Instrumentation and control systems (vibration monitor, discharge pressure sensor, narrow range level auto control) supervised and interpreted by the operator/supervisor.

evidence.quote: vibration monitor ticking up too, still well within the normal band... auto control caught it in seconds
evidence.explanation: Digitally instrumented plant systems generate the readings and automatic corrective actions that the crew monitors and interprets, though the crew does not manually operate mechanical controls in this episode.

task_anchors.task_description: Evaluating an early, within-band pump discharge pressure/vibration oscillation and choosing to log and tighten monitoring rather than escalate.
Consulting the on-call reactor engineer to verify the cause of a brief steam-generator level blip corrected by automatic control.

Choosing a standard continue-and-monitor response for a rising vibration trend while concurrently preparing surveillance pre-brief materials and tracking the ascension schedule, without retrieving available historical comparison data.
Briefly mentioning the vibration trend during an unrelated surveillance pre-brief and deferring fuller review.
